records.title: AI for medical school
records.topics: physiology, pathology and clinical reasoning
records.method: Build a mechanism-first explanation before practising clinical vignettes. Compare your answer with the lecture and an approved reference.
records.prompt: Compare obstructive and restrictive lung disease using this lecture. Ask one question at a time, then explain what I missed.

note.heading: What medical school study asks of you
note.text: Medical school rewards linking a finding to its mechanism: why a lesion causes a sign, why a drug causes a side effect. Lists of buzzwords fall apart when a vignette changes one detail. Use Ace to make you explain the chain out loud, then ask it to change the age, a lab value or the timeline and predict what moves.

question.q: How do I stop memorizing buzzwords without understanding them?
question.a: Ask for the mechanism behind each association before you accept it, then test it on a changed case. If you cannot say why a finding appears, mark it and return to your lecture or an approved reference.

records.title: USMLE Step 1 AI tutor
records.method: Start with the physiological mechanism, predict its effect and then test it in a new vignette.
records.prompt: Explain how a change in preload affects stroke volume. Ask me to predict the direction before explaining the mechanism.

note.heading: Where Step 1 practice usually goes wrong
note.text: The common miss is recognizing a pattern without the mechanism behind it, so a vignette that changes one detail breaks the answer. For every association, ask why: which receptor, enzyme or pathway explains it. Ask Ace to change one variable and predict the result, then confirm with your lecture or an approved reference.

question.q: Can Ace give me official Step 1 questions?
question.a: No. Ace writes original practice from your own material. It is not affiliated with the USMLE or any question bank, and its explanations should be checked against approved references.

records.title: USMLE Step 2 CK AI tutor
records.method: Separate the presentation, discriminating finding and teaching conclusion. Use course references to verify the rationale.
records.prompt: Give me an original practice vignette on this clerkship topic. Ask for the key finding and my reasoning before showing the teaching answer.

note.heading: Where Step 2 CK practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Step 2 CK style questions turn on the next best step, not just the diagnosis. Answers go wrong when the timing, stability or setting in the stem is skipped. Read for those first. Ask Ace to give you a vignette from your notes, commit to a next step and explain why the alternatives come later or not at all.

question.q: How do I practise next-best-step questions?
question.a: Decide the diagnosis, then whether the patient is stable, then the single next action, and say all three out loud. Ask Ace to challenge the order and check management against current, approved references.

records.title: AI for law school
records.topics: case briefs, doctrine and issue spotting
records.method: Brief the assigned opinion before trying a fresh hypothetical. Apply the governing rule to both sides and verify citations against the original authority.
records.prompt: Using this assigned case, separate the facts, issue, holding and reasoning. Give me a new hypothetical that changes one material fact.

note.heading: What law school study asks of you
note.text: Law school tests whether you can find the rule in an opinion and apply it to facts you have not seen. Reading for the holding, separating dicta and arguing both sides matter more than summaries. Use Ace to question your brief and to build hypotheticals that change one fact, then check every rule against the casebook.

question.q: Can AI write my case briefs for me?
question.a: It can check yours. Brief the case yourself first, then ask Ace to compare your issue, holding and reasoning with the opinion on screen. Never rely on an AI citation without reading the source; AI can invent or misstate authority.

records.title: AI for law case briefs
records.focus: facts, issues, holdings and legal reasoning
records.method: Read the opinion first, distinguish holding from dicta and check every quotation against the original.
records.prompt: Brief this assigned opinion using only the text I provide. Separate the holding from dicta and quote the passage supporting each point.

note.heading: Where case briefs usually go wrong
note.text: Briefs go wrong by copying the court’s summary instead of isolating the legally relevant facts, or by stating the holding too broadly. Write the issue as a question the court answered, the holding as its narrow answer and the reasoning as the steps between. Ask Ace to compare your brief with the opinion on screen.

question.q: How long should a case brief be?
question.a: Short enough to use in class, often a few lines per part. Ask Ace which facts you could cut without changing the issue. If a fact does not affect the outcome, it may not belong.

records.title: Bar exam AI study tutor
records.focus: rule recall and essay issue spotting
records.method: State the rule from memory, apply facts on both sides and revise the weak part of your answer.
records.prompt: Give me an original contracts hypothetical. Let me identify the issues and state the rules before grading my analysis.

note.heading: Where bar exam practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Essay answers lose points by missing issues or stating rules vaguely. Recall alone is not enough: you need a rule statement precise enough to apply. Practise writing the rule from memory, then applying it to each fact. Ask Ace for a fact pattern from your outline and have it list the issues you did not raise.

question.q: Can AI grade my bar essays?
question.a: It can give feedback on structure and missed issues, but it is not a grader and can misstate law. Compare its comments with your outline, model answers from your program and the governing rules.

records.title: AI for dental school
records.topics: oral anatomy, pathology and dental cases
records.method: Connect anatomy to a case, explain your reasoning and review the source before turning difficult distinctions into flashcards.
records.prompt: Quiz me on the cranial nerves in this dental anatomy chapter. Ask how each finding changes the case.

note.heading: What dental school study asks of you
note.text: Dental school joins detailed anatomy to clinical decisions: a tooth surface, a nerve or a lesion matters because of what it changes in the case. Practise naming the structure, then explaining its clinical consequence. Ace can quiz you from an anatomy chapter on screen and ask how each finding would change your next step.

question.q: How should I study dental anatomy with AI?
question.a: Use a labelled diagram from your course, cover the labels and ask Ace to quiz you one structure at a time. After each answer, ask why the structure matters clinically, then confirm against the source diagram.

records.title: INBDE AI study tutor
records.method: Link a foundational concept to a finding, explain the connection and review it in your dental course source.
records.prompt: Create an original dental teaching case from this course topic. Ask me to connect the relevant basic science with the findings.

note.heading: Where INBDE practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Integrated questions mix basic science into a clinical case, so studying subjects in isolation leaves gaps. When you review a case, name the science underneath each finding: anatomy, pathology or pharmacology. Ask Ace to turn a chapter into an integrated case and to ask which basic science explains each clinical step.

question.q: How do I study for integrated questions?
question.a: Take one clinical case and list the basic science behind each decision. Ask Ace to quiz you across those links and check each point against your course sources.

records.title: Dental anatomy AI tutor
records.method: Sketch or label the structure before answering; use the source diagram to check your distinction.
records.prompt: Quiz me on tooth morphology from these notes. Ask me to distinguish two similar features and explain their significance.

note.heading: Where dental anatomy study usually goes wrong
note.text: Similar teeth and surfaces blur when you memorize descriptions without comparing them. Study in pairs: two teeth side by side, the features that separate them and how you would tell them apart on a model or image. Ask Ace to quiz you on the distinguishing feature, then check it on your course diagram.

question.q: How do I tell similar teeth apart?
question.a: List the features that differ, not the ones they share, and practise identifying each from a diagram. Ask Ace to quiz you on those differences and confirm with your anatomy text.

records.title: AI for pharmacy school
records.topics: pharmacology, therapeutics and calculations
records.method: Separate mechanism, indication and monitoring in your study notes. Work calculations step by step and verify them with course materials.
records.prompt: Compare these drug classes by mechanism and key distinctions. Test my reasoning without giving the answer first.

note.heading: What pharmacy school study asks of you
note.text: Pharmacy school mixes three kinds of work: drug knowledge, patient-specific therapeutic choices and exact calculations. Each fails differently. Drug facts blur between similar classes, therapeutics needs a reason for every choice and calculations break on units. Ask Ace to keep the three apart, and verify any dose or calculation against your course materials.

question.q: Can I trust AI with pharmacy calculations?
question.a: Use it to check your method, not to replace it. Work the calculation yourself with units on every line, then ask Ace to review each step. Confirm the final number with your course method and references before relying on it.

records.title: NAPLEX AI study tutor
records.method: Write the units at every step, estimate a sensible range and compare the worked solution with the course method.
records.prompt: Make an original calculation exercise from this lesson. Ask for the formula, units and intermediate steps before the result.

note.heading: Where NAPLEX practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Two failure points dominate: calculations that drop a unit or a conversion, and therapeutic choices made without a patient-specific reason. Write units on every line, and for every drug choice say why it suits this patient. Ask Ace to check one step at a time, and confirm doses against your references.

question.q: Can AI check my dosing calculations?
question.a: It can review your steps, but always verify the result with your course method and an authoritative reference. Never use an AI-calculated dose for a real patient.

records.title: Pharmacology AI tutor
records.method: Build a mechanism comparison, test it from memory and verify each distinction against the assigned pharmacology source.
records.prompt: Compare the mechanisms of the classes in these notes. Quiz me on the distinction without introducing an unsupported clinical recommendation.

note.heading: Where pharmacology study usually goes wrong
note.text: Drug facts blur when you learn drugs one at a time. Learn by class: the shared mechanism, then what separates each member. Side effects usually follow from the mechanism, so explain them that way instead of memorizing lists. Ask Ace to compare two classes on screen and test you on the distinctions.

question.q: What is the fastest way to learn drug classes?
question.a: Start with the mechanism for the class, then learn the exceptions. Ask Ace to quiz you on which drug in a class differs and why, and check against your course references.

records.title: AI for veterinary school
records.topics: species differences, veterinary pathology and cases
records.method: Keep species and context explicit. Compare explanations, justify each one and revisit the original teaching case after feedback.
records.prompt: Turn this lecture into a species comparison. Ask which findings change the differential and why.

note.heading: What veterinary school study asks of you
note.text: Veterinary study multiplies every topic by species. A normal value, a drug or an anatomical landmark in a dog may not hold for a horse or a cow. Build comparisons rather than single facts, and always state the species in your prompt. Ace can turn a lecture into a species table and quiz you on the differences.

question.q: Why does the species matter so much in AI prompts?
question.a: Because the right answer often changes with it. Name the species, age and context in every question, and check species-specific facts against your teaching material. A general answer may be right for one species and wrong for another.

records.title: NAVLE AI study tutor
records.method: Name the species, identify the discriminating evidence and review the teaching conclusion using veterinary course references.
records.prompt: Turn this veterinary lesson into an original practice case. Ask which species-specific detail changes the reasoning.

note.heading: Where NAVLE practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Cases go wrong when a fact true for one species is applied to another: normal values, drug safety and common conditions all vary. Read the species and the setting first. Ask Ace to give you a teaching case from your notes, then change only the species and ask what changes in your answer.

question.q: How do I avoid species mix-ups?
question.a: State the species before answering, and keep comparison tables for normal values and drug cautions. Ask Ace to quiz you on the differences and verify them in your course material.

records.title: Veterinary anatomy AI tutor
records.method: Compare named structures across species, then check the comparison against labelled course diagrams.
records.prompt: Quiz me on the anatomical differences between the species in this lecture. Make me explain the functional implication.

note.heading: Where veterinary anatomy study usually goes wrong
note.text: Comparative anatomy is easy to flatten into one generic animal. Exams and clinic ask what differs between species and why it matters. Build tables of the same structure across species and add a clinical consequence for each. Ask Ace to quiz you across species from your lecture and check each answer with your atlas.

question.q: Should I learn one species first?
question.a: Many students anchor on one species, then learn the differences from it. Ask Ace to quiz you on those differences rather than on everything again, and follow your program’s emphasis.

records.title: AI for nursing school
records.topics: clinical judgment, prioritization and care planning
records.method: Practise recognizing cues, prioritizing concerns and explaining your next step. Review rationales rather than memorizing an answer letter.
records.prompt: Give me a practice prioritization question from these notes. Ask who I would assess first and explain the rationale after I answer.

note.heading: What nursing school study asks of you
note.text: Nursing questions ask what you would do first and why. That means recognizing cues, deciding what is most urgent and choosing a safe next action, not recalling a single fact. Practise explaining your priority out loud. Ace can give you a practice scenario from your notes and ask for your rationale before it shares any teaching points.

question.q: How can AI help with prioritization questions?
question.a: Ask Ace for a practice scenario based on your notes, answer with your first action and your reason, then compare its feedback with your course framework. The value is in explaining the rationale, not in collecting answer letters.

records.title: NCLEX AI study help
records.method: Identify cues, rank concerns and justify a response. Compare the rationale with the course framework.
records.prompt: Write an original prioritization exercise from this nursing topic. Ask which cue matters most and why before explaining the answer.

note.heading: Where NCLEX practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Prioritization answers often go wrong by choosing a correct action that is not the first action. Look for the cue that signals the most immediate risk and the safest next step. Practise saying who you would assess first and why. Ask Ace for scenarios from your notes and have it question your rationale before revealing teaching points.

question.q: Does Ace use real NCLEX questions?
question.a: No. Ace writes original practice from your material and has no affiliation with the NCLEX or its owners. Check rationales against your course frameworks and approved review resources.

records.title: AI for nursing care plan study
records.method: Use a fictional or de-identified course case, separate observations from assumptions and make the evaluation criteria specific.
records.prompt: Use this fictional teaching case to help me connect assessment cues, a nursing goal and how the goal would be evaluated.

note.heading: Where care-plan practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Care plans go wrong when interventions do not connect to the assessment data or the stated goal. Each intervention should trace back to a cue and forward to a measurable outcome. Practise on fictional cases from your course. Ask Ace to check whether each intervention has a reason and a way to evaluate it.

question.q: Can AI write a care plan for me?
question.a: For learning, write it yourself and ask Ace to check the links between data, diagnosis, interventions and outcomes. Follow your program’s format, and never enter real patient information.

records.title: AI for physician assistant school
records.topics: history taking, differentials and clinical cases
records.method: Start with a concise presentation, identify discriminating findings and explain what supports each possibility using your course sources.
records.prompt: Use this rotation topic for a clinical vignette. Let me explain the differential before showing teaching points.

note.heading: What physician assistant study asks of you
note.text: PA training moves quickly across specialties, so the core skill is an organized approach: a focused history, a short differential and the finding that separates the options. Rotations add case presentations. Use Ace to rehearse a concise presentation and to push you to name the one finding that changes your leading diagnosis.

question.q: How do I practise case presentations alone?
question.a: Present a de-identified teaching case out loud to Ace in a fixed order, then ask which details were missing or out of order. Keep presentations short and repeat with a new case rather than polishing one.

records.title: PANCE AI study tutor
records.method: Present a concise answer, justify the important evidence and review why each alternative fits less well.
records.prompt: Ask an original practice question on this PA course topic. Let me explain why I rejected the alternatives.

note.heading: Where PANCE practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Broad exams invite shallow review. The common miss is stopping at the likely diagnosis without the finding that rules out the close alternative. Practise naming the discriminating finding for each pair of look-alike conditions. Ask Ace to quiz you on those pairs from your notes and confirm answers with your course references.

question.q: How do I cover so many topics?
question.a: Prioritize by your program’s blueprint and your weak areas. Short, mixed quizzes from your own notes help; ask Ace for a few questions per topic and track what you miss.

records.title: AI for PA clinical rotations
records.method: Organize the presentation around relevant positives and negatives, then identify gaps to discuss with your instructor.
records.prompt: Use this de-identified teaching case to rehearse a one-minute presentation. Ask what information is missing.

note.heading: Where rotation presentations usually go wrong
note.text: Presentations go wrong by including everything. Preceptors want the pertinent positives and negatives that support your assessment, in a predictable order. Practise trimming. Present a de-identified teaching case out loud to Ace and ask which details you could cut and which missing finding would change the plan.

question.q: How do I prepare for a new rotation?
question.a: Review the common presentations for that specialty and practise one short case presentation per topic. Ask Ace to quiz you on the key differentials, and follow your preceptor’s preferred format.

records.title: AI for optometry school
records.topics: vision science, optics and ocular cases
records.method: Move between the diagram, optical principle and calculation. Check units and assumptions against your lecture notes.
records.prompt: Quiz me on this optics lesson. Make me explain the sign convention and calculation steps before revealing the solution.

note.heading: What optometry school study asks of you
note.text: Optometry pairs clinical reasoning with optics problems where one sign or unit error ruins the answer. Work optics with a sketch and a stated sign convention every time. For ocular cases, connect what you see on examination with the likely cause. Ace can quiz you on each calculation step before showing the worked solution.

question.q: Why do I keep getting optics problems wrong?
question.a: Usually a sign convention or unit slips partway through. Write the convention at the top, label each distance and ask Ace to check one step at a time instead of the final answer. Confirm the method with your course notes.

records.title: NBEO AI study tutor
records.method: Explain the principle before applying it, and use the optometry course reference to check the result.
records.prompt: Turn these optometry notes into an original recall question. Ask me to connect the principle to its application.

note.heading: Where NBEO practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Optometry exams mix clinical recognition with calculation, and each needs a different check. For clinical items, name the finding before the diagnosis. For calculations, state the formula and units first. Ask Ace to quiz you across both from your course notes and to stop you when you skip a step.

question.q: Is Ace connected to the NBEO?
question.a: No. Ace writes original practice from your course material and is not affiliated with any exam provider. Use your program’s resources to confirm exam scope.

records.title: Optometry optics AI tutor
records.method: Draw the optical system, state the convention and track units through the calculation.
records.prompt: Work through this optics exercise with me. Ask me to define the sign convention before we calculate.

note.heading: Where optics problems usually go wrong
note.text: Most optics errors are sign errors. Light direction, object and image distances and lens power each carry a sign, and switching conventions mid-problem ruins the result. Sketch the ray diagram, write the convention and label every distance. Ask Ace to check one step at a time instead of only the final number.

question.q: What sign convention should I use?
question.a: Use the one your course teaches and write it at the top of every problem. Ask Ace to follow that convention explicitly, and check worked examples from your course.

records.title: AI for physical therapy school
records.topics: movement analysis, rehabilitation and examination
records.method: Explain an impairment in terms of function, compare examination findings and review the reasoning behind your answer.
records.prompt: Use this rehabilitation case to quiz my movement analysis. Ask which finding changes my working explanation.

note.heading: What physical therapy study asks of you
note.text: Physical therapy study links anatomy to movement and function. Knowing a muscle’s attachments is the start; explaining what weakness or restriction does to gait, reaching or a transfer is the point. Practise describing findings in functional terms. Ace can quiz you from a rehabilitation case and ask which finding would change your explanation.

question.q: How do I connect anatomy to function?
question.a: For each structure, ask what movement it produces, what happens when it is weak or restricted and which daily task shows it. Ask Ace to quiz you in that order and check answers against your course texts.

records.title: NPTE AI study tutor
records.method: Separate the movement observation from the hypothesis and review the strongest supporting finding.
records.prompt: Create an original movement-analysis question from this lesson. Ask which finding best supports my explanation.

note.heading: Where NPTE practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Questions often ask for the most appropriate intervention or the next examination step. Answers go wrong by choosing something reasonable that does not fit the patient’s stage, precautions or goal. Read those first. Ask Ace for a case from your notes and have it question whether your choice fits that stage.

question.q: Does Ace know current physical therapy guidelines?
question.a: It can explain concepts, but guidelines change and AI can be out of date. Check interventions and precautions against your course materials and current references.

records.title: Physical therapy anatomy AI tutor
records.method: Connect structure to function and check the explanation with the course anatomy diagram.
records.prompt: Quiz me on the muscles and actions in these notes. Ask how changing the joint position changes the explanation.

note.heading: Where functional anatomy study usually goes wrong
note.text: Learning origins and insertions without function makes anatomy hard to use. For each muscle, name the movement, the task where you see it and what weakness looks like. Ask Ace to quiz you in that order from your lecture, and to describe a functional problem so you work back to the structure.

question.q: How do I make anatomy stick?
question.a: Tie each structure to a movement you can perform and a daily task. Ask Ace to quiz you on function as well as names, and review with your course atlas.

records.title: AI for occupational therapy school
records.topics: occupational performance and activity analysis
records.method: Keep the person, occupation and environment connected. Compare adaptations and support your reasoning with the assigned framework.
records.prompt: Turn this course case into an activity analysis. Ask me to connect the client goal, task demands and environment.

note.heading: What occupational therapy study asks of you
note.text: Occupational therapy keeps three things in view at once: the person, the activity and the environment. Many study answers fail by fixing one and ignoring the others. Practise activity analysis on ordinary tasks, then adapt one element at a time. Ace can ask you to justify each adaptation against the client goal in your course case.

question.q: What is a good way to practise activity analysis?
question.a: Pick an everyday task, break it into steps and demands, then ask Ace to change the client or the setting. Explain how your plan changes and check your reasoning against the framework your program uses.

records.title: NBCOT AI study tutor
records.method: Describe the goal, examine the activity demands and justify your answer using the assigned OT framework.
records.prompt: Give me an original OT teaching scenario. Ask me to connect the occupational goal with the task demands.

note.heading: Where NBCOT practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Case questions go wrong when the answer fixes the impairment and forgets the client’s goal or setting. Read for the occupation the client cares about and the context they live in. Ask Ace for a case from your notes and have it ask how your choice serves that goal, then check your framework.

question.q: Is Ace affiliated with NBCOT?
question.a: No. Ace writes original study practice from your material and has no exam-provider affiliation. Use your program’s resources to confirm exam content.

records.title: OT activity analysis AI tutor
records.method: Break the activity into observable steps and compare potential adaptations against the stated goal.
records.prompt: Help me analyze this fictional daily activity. Ask about the person, task and environment one at a time.

note.heading: Where activity analysis usually goes wrong
note.text: Activity analysis goes wrong when it lists steps without the demands each step places on the person. For each step, name the physical, cognitive and environmental demands, then what changes for your client. Ask Ace to change one element, such as the setting, and explain how your adaptation changes.

question.q: What tasks are good for practice?
question.a: Ordinary ones: making tea, dressing, using a phone. Break the task into steps and demands, then ask Ace to change the client or setting and question your adaptation.

records.title: AI for podiatry school
records.topics: lower-limb anatomy, biomechanics and cases
records.method: Trace anatomy into biomechanics, distinguish similar findings and check your explanation against the source diagram.
records.prompt: Ask me to connect this anatomy lesson with a gait finding. Wait for my explanation before giving feedback.

note.heading: What podiatry school study asks of you
note.text: Podiatry study runs from detailed lower-limb anatomy into biomechanics and gait. A finding at the foot often reflects something higher up the chain, so practise tracing it both ways. Ace can quiz you on an anatomy diagram and then ask how a structural change would show up in the gait cycle.

question.q: How should I study gait with AI?
question.a: Describe one phase of gait at a time, name the structures doing the work and ask Ace what changes if one is impaired. Compare its answer with your course diagrams rather than accepting a general description.

records.title: APMLE AI study tutor
records.method: Use an anatomical explanation for each answer and compare it with the assigned podiatry reference.
records.prompt: Create a recall drill from this podiatry topic. Ask me to connect each finding with the relevant anatomy.

note.heading: Where APMLE practice usually goes wrong
note.text: Broad exam review tends to drift toward familiar topics. Track the areas you miss and return to them with focused practice. For lower-limb cases, connect the finding to the structure and the mechanism. Ask Ace to quiz you on your weakest topics from your notes and check answers against your course sources.

question.q: Is Ace connected to the APMLE?
question.a: No. Ace writes original practice from your course material and is not affiliated with the exam. Confirm exam scope with your program.

records.title: Podiatry biomechanics AI tutor
records.method: Describe the observed pattern before proposing a mechanism, then check it against the source diagram.
records.prompt: Quiz me on this gait diagram. Ask which movement or structure explains the pattern I identify.

note.heading: Where biomechanics study usually goes wrong
note.text: Biomechanics goes wrong when the foot is studied in isolation. Changes at the foot can come from, or cause, changes at the ankle, knee and hip. Trace a finding up and down the chain. Ask Ace to quiz you on one phase of gait at a time and to ask what compensates when a structure fails.

question.q: How do I study the gait cycle?
question.a: Learn the phases in order, the structures active in each and the common compensations. Ask Ace to quiz you phase by phase and compare with your course diagrams.

records.title: AI for chiropractic school
records.topics: anatomy and musculoskeletal reasoning
records.method: Review anatomy before interpretation. Distinguish what a teaching case establishes from what needs further examination.
records.prompt: Create a recall drill from this spinal anatomy lesson. Ask about landmarks and the reasoning behind each association.

note.heading: What chiropractic school study asks of you
note.text: Chiropractic study leans heavily on anatomy: spinal landmarks, nerve relationships and musculoskeletal structure. Recall drills help, but exams and clinic ask you to reason from those structures. Ace can run quick recall from a lesson on screen and then ask what each landmark means for examination findings.

question.q: Is AI useful for anatomy recall drills?
question.a: Yes, for practice. Ask Ace to quiz you from your own lesson, one item at a time, and to say whether you were right. Keep a list of misses and review them with the original material.

records.title: NBCE AI study tutor
records.method: Link recall to reasoning and use the assigned course text to resolve uncertain points.
records.prompt: Ask original review questions from this chiropractic lecture. Require an explanation rather than a one-word answer.

note.heading: Where NBCE review usually goes wrong
note.text: Review goes wrong when recall stays separate from reasoning. After a recall drill, ask how the structure shows up in examination or imaging. Keep teaching cases distinct from what you would need to confirm in a real examination. Ask Ace to quiz you from your notes and to push from recall into reasoning.

question.q: Does Ace use real NBCE questions?
question.a: No. Ace writes original practice from your material and has no affiliation with the exam provider. Confirm content with your program’s resources.

records.title: Spinal anatomy AI tutor
records.method: Locate the landmark, explain its relationship to nearby structures and verify with a labelled diagram.
records.prompt: Quiz me on the vertebral landmarks in these notes. Ask what passes through the named structure.

note.heading: Where spinal anatomy study usually goes wrong
note.text: Regional differences between vertebrae and the relationship of nerves to landmarks are where most errors happen. Compare one vertebra from each region side by side and trace each nerve root to where it exits. Ask Ace to quiz you on distinguishing features and on what a problem at each level would affect.

question.q: How do I learn the vertebral regions?
question.a: Study what makes each region distinct and practise identifying vertebrae from images. Ask Ace to quiz you on those features and check against your atlas.

records.title: AI for public health school
records.topics: epidemiology, biostatistics and population health
records.method: State the population and study design, calculate the measure with units and discuss the limits of the inference.
records.prompt: Ask me to identify the study design, possible bias and measure of association in this epidemiology problem.

note.heading: What public health study asks of you
note.text: Public health questions often turn on the study design: who was sampled, what was compared and what can be concluded. Many wrong answers come from over-reading a result. Name the design and the population first, then the measure and its limits. Ace can ask you to spot bias and confounding before it explains the problem.

question.q: How do I avoid over-interpreting study results?
question.a: State the design, the population and the comparison before reading the result. Then ask Ace what the study cannot show. Check definitions and formulas against your course materials.

records.title: Epidemiology AI tutor
records.method: State the population, exposure and outcome before classifying the design or interpreting an association.
records.prompt: Give me a short study description. Ask me to identify the design and one plausible source of bias.

note.heading: Where epidemiology problems usually go wrong
note.text: Problems go wrong when the design is misidentified, because the design decides which measure and which conclusions are valid. Name the design first: cohort, case-control, cross-sectional or trial. Then name the likeliest bias. Ask Ace for a problem from your lesson and have it question your design call before you calculate.

question.q: How do I tell study designs apart?
question.a: Ask how participants were selected and when exposure and outcome were measured. Ask Ace to quiz you with short study descriptions and check definitions in your course text.

records.title: Biostatistics AI tutor
records.method: Identify the quantity being estimated, interpret uncertainty and keep association separate from causation.
records.prompt: Use this course example to quiz me on the estimate, uncertainty and what the result does not establish.

note.heading: Where biostatistics usually goes wrong
note.text: Interpretation errors are more common than arithmetic ones: reading a p-value as the chance the result is true, or treating a confidence interval as a range of individual values. Say in plain words what each number means. Ask Ace to quiz you on interpretation from your lesson, and check definitions in your course text.

question.q: Can AI do my statistics homework?

records.title: AI for business school

records.title: AI for graduate school

records.title: AI for reading research papers

note.text: Readers often accept the abstract’s claim without checking whether the method supports it. question.q: Can AI summarize papers for me?

records.title: AI for qualifying exam study

note.heading: Where qualifying exam prep usually goes wrong
note.text: Preparation goes wrong when you rehearse what you know instead of what you will be asked. Committees probe the edges: alternative explanations, limitations and foundations. question.q: How should I practise for an oral exam?
question.a: Explain a topic out loud for a few minutes, then ask Ace to interrupt with a challenging question. Note what you could not answer and return to your sources.

note.heading: Where ethics analysis usually goes wrong
note.text: Ethics answers go wrong when a personal value stands in for the professional standard, or when only one obligation is weighed. records.title: AI for teacher education

question.q: Does Ace have official Praxis questions?

records.title: AI for lesson plan study

note.heading: Where lesson plans usually go wrong

records.title: AI for psychology school

records.title: EPPP AI study tutor

note.heading: Where EPPP review usually goes wrong

question.q: Is Ace connected to the EPPP?
question.a: No. Ace writes original study practice from your material and has no exam-provider affiliation. Confirm content with your program’s resources.

records.title: Counseling theory AI tutor

note.heading: Where comparing theories usually goes wrong

question.q: How do I compare counseling theories?
question.a: Use the same fictional case for each theory and compare the explanation and plan each produces. Ask Ace to check your summaries against your assigned readings.

records.title: AI for accounting school

records.title: HVAC school AI study tutor

records.prompt: Turn these lecture notes into five questions. Wait for my answer before showing the explanation.

note.heading: Where lecture notes usually go wrong
note.text: Notes go wrong when they copy slides word for word and are never used again. Better notes capture the main ideas in your words and become questions you can answer later. After a lecture, ask Ace to turn your notes into recall questions and quiz you a day later, then again a few days after that.

question.q: Can Ace take notes in my lectures?
question.a: Ace can make notes and flashcards from a lecture it hears through your computer’s microphone. Follow your school’s and instructor’s rules on recording, and review the notes against the lecture slides.

records.title: AI for college exam study
records.method: Prioritize syllabus topics, practise retrieval and verify explanations against the assigned material.
records.prompt: Use my syllabus topics to quiz me one question at a time. Ask me to explain the idea in my own words.

note.heading: Where exam study usually goes wrong
note.text: Rereading feels productive but tests poorly. Practise retrieving the material instead: answer questions without notes, then check. Spread sessions over days rather than one long night. Ask Ace to quiz you from your course notes and mix topics, so you practise choosing the right method as well as using it.

question.q: How far ahead should I start studying for an exam?
question.a: Earlier and spread out beats one long session. Start with short daily quizzes from your notes and use the last days to review what you miss most often.
